blocks.html: When google.com is typed

blocks.html: Browser checks its own cache to get the IP
blocks.text: Browser checks its own cache to get the IP

blocks.html: If the IP is not found in browser cache, it makes an operating system, which in most cases its own cache
blocks.text: If the IP is not found in browser cache, it makes an operating system, which in most cases its own cache

blocks.html: If the IP is not found there too, then call goes to DNS resolver, which has its own cache.
blocks.text: If the IP is not found there too, then call goes to DNS resolver, which has its own cache.

blocks.html: If the IP could not be found or the entry in the DNS resolver’s cache is expired, the call goes to root nameservers, which respond with the list of TLD name servers.
blocks.text: If the IP could not be found or the entry in the DNS resolver’s cache is expired, the call goes to root nameservers, which respond with the list of TLD name servers.

blocks.html: Then the call goes to the TLD nameserver (.com in this example), which returns the authoritative nameservers to the google.com
blocks.text: Then the call goes to the TLD nameserver (.com in this example), which returns the authoritative nameservers to the google.com

blocks.html: Then the call goes to the authoritative name server, which finally returns the IP address of the google.com to the DNS resolver.
blocks.text: Then the call goes to the authoritative name server, which finally returns the IP address of the google.com to the DNS resolver.

blocks.html: Then the IP is returned to the OS.
blocks.text: Then the IP is returned to the OS.

blocks.html: OS then returns to the browser.
